correctness.rationale: The fair two-state generator gives f''+2λf'+v²f=0 and the displayed closed solutions. Combining the unital-qubit Pauli multipliers (e^{-κt}f,e^{-κt}f,e^{-κt}) with Ruskai's criterion gives the exact equivalence |f|>(e^{κt}-1)/2. In every postzero oscillatory lobe log(|f|/h_κ) has strictly negative second derivative because -ω² csc²(ω(t-z_j))+[κ/(2sinh(κt/2))]²<-ω²+1/t²<0. Hence each lobe has one or zero non-entanglement-breaking intervals. The π/ω translation strictly reduces each threshold. Evaluation at the unique amplitude extremum bounds κ_j between log(1+2e^{-λt_j})/t_j and that numerator divided by z_j. These bounds rigorously yield λ>0 Lambert-W counting with O(1) index error and λ=0 inverse-κ counting; λ≥v has a monotone coherence function and only one EB crossing. The standalone matrix-exponential/Choi partial-transpose checks reproduced the exact finite formulas. Finite checks are supportive, not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: Existing literature explicitly contains the unital-qubit EB criterion, telegraph-coherence formulas and the qualitative finite revival phenomenon with relaxation. Full-text comparison of the four directly relevant works distinguishes the indexed, strictly decreasing entanglement-breaking-revival thresholds and the precise Lambert-function count (including negative log-log correction) from their statements. Equivalent Choi/singular-value formulations and qualitative finite-revival implications were considered; the nearest old result does not resolve the exact new parameter-dependent maxima. Targeted mathematical-record searches were also conducted without a matching published record, but absence of search results is not a novelty proof. Residual risk: a stronger, unidentified channel-evolution theorem might imply the threshold optimization or quantitative rate law. Independently assessed priority remains unverified.

value.rationale: The exact number of entanglement-preserving revivals in a telegraph-noisy qubit with an independent weak Markovian depolarizer is an interpretable operational quantity, not merely a special-function exercise. Strictly ordered lobe thresholds distinguish oscillatory coherence from actual entanglement-transmission capacity, while the negative log-log correction to the positive-switching logarithmic law and the singular inverse-rate law of static noise give sharp, potentially testable design scales. Published work already observes qualitative death/revival and finite return under relaxation; the object of value is the all-lobe classification and sharp number-of-revivals asymptotic, not the known base dynamics. No general hardware efficiency or experimental precision claims are made.
